name: Blob URLs (object URLs)
plain: Makes a temporary URL for in-memory data or a File, usable in links, images and downloads.
meaning: A site can hand files to itself without a server round trip. The URL works only in that browser and origin and dies when the page unloads or is revoked.

access.persistence: Until the document unloads or revokeObjectURL() is called
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Same origin only; partitioned by top level site in modern browsers
steps: Create a Blob or take a File
Use the blob: URL in img, a download or fetch

limits.headline: Can make temporary links to data held in memory, which work only on its own site
limits.user_action: You pick an image to preview, or tap Download for a file the page built.
can: Turn a file or data into a temporary link for images, video or downloads
Preview an image you chose before upload
Hand you a file it built, for you to download
cannot: Open files you did not pick or that it did not build
Use the link from another site, since it only works on the site that made it
Keep the link after you close the tab

story.what_it_is: Makes a temporary web address for data held in memory or a file you chose.

marketing.name: URL.createObjectURL
marketing.pitch: Documents how a page can turn a file or data into a short lived address for images, videos and downloads.

story.for_you: You see a photo preview appear the moment you pick it, or a download start for a file the page just made. The page never sent it anywhere first.
story.for_makers: It lets a site show or save data without uploading it. That makes previews instant and tools faster. It can also hide files from simple scanners, so security teams watch for it.

use_cases.example: You choose a photo for a profile and see it right away, before it uploads.
A web editor lets you download your edited image or video straight from memory.
A browser game saves and shares a replay or screenshot as a downloaded file.
A web video tool plays a clip you recorded without sending it to a server.
A document site makes a PDF in your browser and offers it as a download.
A phishing page builds a fake document in memory and shows it from a blob address so filters do not see it.
A chat site previews an attachment the second you pick it.

technical_bounds: Only usable by the origin that created it (fetching from another origin fails)
Top frame navigation to blob: and data: URLs from other origins is blocked (Chrome 60, Firefox 59 for data:)
Not a persistent store: gone after reload or unload; unrevoked URLs keep the Blob in memory
Chrome stores big blobs on disk; practical single blob sizes of a few gigabytes
Blob URL storage partitioning by top level site is rolling out across browsers (Firefox and Safari first, Chrome later)

abuse: Phishing pages built from blob URLs that hide the real host

history.change: Block top frame navigation to blob and data URLs from other origins
Blob URL partitioning by top level site (rollout date approximate)
